topics.title: Urban and rural areas, and population density

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish urban areas from rural areas by population, occupations, infrastructure and local governing bodies.
Calculate and compare population density as the number of people per square kilometre.

topics.title: How cities become centres of economic activity
topics.ncert_sections: How do Cities Become Centres of Economic Activities?; What Leads to Urbanisation?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how location near rivers, coasts, trade routes or raw materials helps a place grow into a city, as in Jamshedpur.
Describe urbanisation and the stages by which a rural area turns into a metropolitan area.

topics.title: Economic hubs and specialised cities
topics.ncert_sections: Mumbai, Bengaluru, smaller urban centres, Agra, Varanasi and Delhi

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how institutions, clusters of industries and education helped cities like Mumbai and Bengaluru become hubs.
Identify smaller urban centres known for particular industries and why firms locate in growing cities.
Analyse how historical, cultural and pilgrimage sites drive economic activity and livelihoods in cities.
Explain how cities mix cultures, food and festivals, using examples such as vada pav and Kolkata's Durga Puja.
Describe how cultural centres, museums, libraries and stadiums help city residents interact and form networks.
Identify the pressures that growing populations put on city infrastructure, air quality and safety.
Explain why slums grow in cities, how slum dwellers support the city, and how housing schemes respond.
Evaluate how collective action revived Bengaluru's lakes and eased its water crisis.

topics.title: Planning our cities: the Pink City of Jaipur

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors urban planners must consider, such as jobs, transport, land use and public safety.
Describe the planning features of Jaipur and how they suited security, trade, aesthetics and the dry climate.
Explain how Singapore's Concept Plan and Master Plan make its long-term planning flexible.
Analyse how mixed-use spaces, public transport and vertical gardens give dense Singapore a good quality of life.

topics.title: Urban redevelopment and sustainable cities of tomorrow
topics.ncert_sections: Urban redevelopment in India; concluding section

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Indian redevelopment projects such as the Sabarmati Riverfront and Gangtok's M.G. Road.
Evaluate how technology and sustainable planning can balance city growth with care for people and Nature.
